evidence: `void full.subscribe(...)` with no handler can reject unhandled, so the premise holds. The fix `.catch(() => undefined)` turns a failed size subscription into silence: the pane would never resize and nothing would report it.
guidance_note: When a fire-and-forget promise needs a rejection handler, send the failure somewhere observable (a logger, a state field, an error event) instead of copying the reviewer's `.catch(() => undefined)`.

evidence: The hunk shows a template literal containing `" +` and a newline followed by `"must precede...`, so the quote characters end up in the message text. Collapsing it into one template string is the right fix.
guidance_note: Run a failing case of every custom assertion message once before committing, so a malformed message shows up in its own output.

evidence: The header says bench:gate wires --expose-gc "in 8w9.5+", but the reviewer notes this same PR already sets NODE_OPTIONS=--expose-gc in package.json. The agent's comment update matches that.
guidance_note: When a PR implements something a comment describes as future work, grep for the ticket id (here 8w9.5) and update every comment that still calls it pending.

narrative: There was one Copilot round with three findings, all valid, and all were accepted in 0b0838c. Two were small consistency fixes (a malformed assertion message and a stale comment). The third, an unhandled subscribe rejection, was fixed by silently swallowing the error, which hides a failed size subscription.
guidance_observations: The agent justified the silent catch by pointing at a matching catch in dispose(). Copying an existing swallow pattern spreads a silent failure instead of fixing it.

evidence: In detached mode, output is only counted, and the fast path replays `this.lastSeed` without checking for it. So attach, detach, more output, then re-attach paints a stale screen and loses those bytes. The fix nulls lastSeed on detached output and adds a test for that sequence.
guidance_note: When adding a cache, list every event that makes the cached value stale (reconnect, output while detached, failed fill) before writing the fast path, and add an invalidation and a test for each.

evidence: The hunk writes `this.lastSeed = { captured, cursor }` after a catch that leaves `captured` empty, so a failed seed would be cached and replayed. Gating the write on success and adding a test is correct.
guidance_note: Only write a cache on the success path; a catch that falls through to the cache write turns one transient failure into a permanent one.

evidence: The isVisible doc says "BufferingSink hard-codes `true`", while the same PR gives BufferingSink a `visible` option and `setVisible()`.
guidance_note: When an interface doc describes a specific implementation's behavior, check that implementation in the same PR before committing the doc.

evidence: The NOTE says "current PaneStream implementation re-seeds on every attach... lands as part of this ticket", but this PR implements the cache. The reply-hint says pushback, but the agent actually rewrote the note.
guidance_note: After implementing what a stub test's TODO note describes, delete or rewrite the note in the same commit that turns the test green.

narrative: This PR auto-closed when its base branch was deleted, and its four findings were fixed in #22 (7f2e7ca). There were two real cache-correctness bugs in the new re-attach fast path (stale seed after detached output, failed seed cached) and two stale docs.
guidance_observations: The cache-invalidation bugs were found by the reviewer, not by the author. A list of every event that invalidates the cache, made before adding the fast path, would have caught both.

evidence: The class header documents that methods no-op after dispose(), and `setVisible` was the one mutator without the `isDisposed` guard. The fix adds the guard and a test.
guidance_note: When a class documents a post-dispose no-op contract, check every public mutator against it, including the test-only helpers.

evidence: This round reviewed 7f2e7ca, the commit named as the fix for #21/F1. That fix added the comment "idle/detached: ... We also null out lastSeed", but the code nulls it only in the detached branch.
guidance_note: When a fix adds a branch-specific action under a combined comment label like idle/detached, split the label so the comment says which branch does it.

evidence: The lifecycle doc still says `seed(text, cursor)` / `write(bytes)` after the interface was renamed to `seed(captured, cursor)` / `write(data)` in the original change. This is cosmetic but accurate, and was not caused by a fix.
guidance_note: When renaming parameters in an interface, grep the file's doc comments for the old names in the same edit.

evidence: The original change added `clear()` and `isVisible()` to TerminalSink, and the test RecordingSink was not updated; the agent confirmed that tests are not type-checked, which is why this went unnoticed. The drift dates from the interface change, not from the #21 fix.
guidance_note: When adding methods to an interface whose test fakes are outside the typecheck graph, grep for every `implements`/fake of it and update them, since the compiler will not.

narrative: This is a redo of #21, carrying the fixes for #21's four findings. Its single round found one comment drift caused by the #21/F1 fix (the idle/detached label) and three other small contract/doc gaps from the original change. All were accepted in e2a267d.
guidance_observations: Test files outside tsc let a stale test fake (RecordingSink) survive an interface change. Including tests in a typecheck would turn this class of finding into a build error.

evidence: The real problem was that the header comment said every xterm/DOM detail lives behind TerminalSink, which contradicted the public `readonly terminal`. The agent says the ticket's contract names that field as API, so it kept the field and narrowed the comment to the producer-to-renderer seam (b119a7d).
guidance_note: When a header comment cites a seam law, check that the class's public surface actually matches the claim before committing it.

evidence: `if (this.isDisposed) return` at the top of dispose() makes `terminal.dispose()` run at most once, so the bare catch could only hide real failures. The agent confirms the catch was copied from the demo and removed it.
guidance_note: When porting code from a prototype into a library wrapper, recheck every try/catch against the wrapper's own guards instead of keeping the prototype's reasons.

evidence: "within 1MB" reads as inclusive, so `toBeLessThan` is off by one at exactly the budget. As the agent notes, that boundary never occurs on a noisy heap measurement, so the fix matters little either way.

The flag is a false positive: b119a7d only touched xterm-sink/index.ts and the g6 bench, and font-cache.ts is unchanged since round 0. The packet shows no environment where `document.fonts` exists but is null, and the agent's "trust boundary" argument for the guard is about a hypothetical shim, which is exactly what the cited law warns against.
guidance_note: Before accepting a null guard for a hypothetical environment, name the concrete runtime (happy-dom version, polyfill) where the value is null; if none can be named, push back.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: b119a7d did not touch g1-attach-paint.bench.ts, so this round reviewed pre-existing code. Today `uniqueSocket()` is synchronous and cannot fail before the assignment, but an unguarded `tmux -L undefined kill-server` could reach a real server, so the cheap guard is defensible.
guidance_note: When a test teardown runs a destructive command against a resource name, initialize the name to a sentinel and skip the command when setup never assigned it.

narrative: Round 0 raised three findings on the new XtermSink, all handled reasonably in b119a7d. Round 1 is flagged as on that fix commit, but both of its findings are in files b119a7d did not touch (font-cache.ts, the g1 bench). They are new looks at pre-existing code, not fallout from the fix. The F4 null guard was accepted for a hypothetical shim.
guidance_observations: The agent said it would file follow-up tickets for the same socket-guard gap in two other integration test files; the packet does not show whether that happened.
Re-review flags on a fix commit can come purely from the PR's head moving forward; read the commit's file list before attributing round-1 findings to the fix.

evidence: An async function's body runs synchronously up to its first await, so `this.seed()` executes before the assignment to `pendingSeed`; the docstring's "BEFORE the body executes" was false. The agent rewrote it to state the actual ordering.
guidance_note: When a comment makes a claim about async ordering, trace the sync prefix of the async call before writing it.

evidence: `void props.stream.sendKeys(data)` can reject unhandled. The agent added `.catch(() => undefined)` and argued that transport failures surface via connectionState. That covers a dropped connection, but a command-level rejection would vanish, and the packet does not show which kinds of rejection sendKeys can produce.
guidance_note: Before swallowing a promise rejection on the grounds that another channel reports it, check that every kind of rejection actually reaches that channel.

evidence: This is the same `void stream.sendKeys(data)` pattern in the vanilla adapter, with the same swallow-and-point-at-connectionState fix. It has the same open question as F2: non-transport rejections are dropped silently.
guidance_note: When the same promise call appears in two sibling adapters, route both through one shared helper so the error policy is decided once.

narrative: There was one round with three findings, accepted in 4e05e48: an inaccurate async-ordering docstring and two unhandled sendKeys rejections. The rejections were swallowed, with a stated reason that is plausible for transport loss but unverified for other failures.
guidance_observations: This is the third PR in the batch (#20, #24) where an unhandled-rejection finding was settled with `.catch(() => undefined)`; the agent has a default of silencing rather than routing errors.

evidence: `isActive` was computed from `Date.now()` during render, with nothing to trigger a re-render when the TTL ran out. Instead of the suggested forced re-render, the agent made `isActive` an observable reset by a timer (381b024), which is a cleaner design than the suggestion.
guidance_note: Never derive displayed state from `Date.now()` in an observer render; model a time-based expiry as an observable that a timer resets.

evidence: This duplicates F1, raised in round 1 on the same commit b90f24c before any fix landed. It was settled by the same fix, 381b024.

The agent agreed that two lockfiles break single source of truth, then resolved the thread with no change, saying it was "surfacing to the user". The issue was raised twice more (F7, F9). Later commits move scripts and publish.yml to pnpm, so the eventual answer was a full migration that could have been made at this point.
guidance_note: When a reviewer finds two competing sources of truth that the branch itself introduced, pick one and finish the migration in this PR instead of resolving the thread while waiting for a decision.

evidence: The agent's eight-step trace shows bytes buffered during the second seeding window landing in seed2's snapshot and then being replayed from the buffer. Clearing the buffer before `startSeedCycle()` fixes it (8c4d043). The coalescing code was in the PR from round 0, so no fix caused this.
guidance_note: When adding a re-issue path to a buffered seed, decide which seed cycle the buffer belongs to and reset it at the point the new capture is issued.

evidence: The header said gates are "exercised through BridgePaneStreamClient" while the file only builds DirectPaneStreamClient. The reviewer offered fixing either the code or the header; the agent fixed the header. The reply-hint says pushback, but the reply accepts.
guidance_note: Write a file header after the implementation, describing what the file actually builds, not what was planned.

evidence: The agent quotes `src/client.ts`: a spawn-style TmuxClient "never emits `reconnected`", so wiring it would be dead code. That makes the reviewer's claim that reconnect gates measured this way would be wrong moot, but the silent no-op branch deserved an explanatory comment.
guidance_note: When an interface method is deliberately a no-op in an implementation, write the comment saying why at the time you write the method.

evidence: This repeats F3 (raised on the same commit 381b024 as round 2), and the agent again deferred to the user. Same verdict as F3.
This duplicates F4 on the same commit and was fixed by the same buffer clear in 8c4d043.

This is the third time the lockfile issue was raised. The agent called it "already resolved with pushback", but no change had been made, and a thread resolved without a change does not resolve two lockfiles. This round happened only because F3 was left open.
guidance_note: A finding re-raised three times shows a resolution that changed nothing; settle it in code.

evidence: The npm-to-pnpm move, the eventual answer to the lockfile threads, converted `dev`/`dev:watch`/`demo:electron` but left `start:web: npm run dev`. 444c323 finished the sweep seconds before this review. The packet does not show which commit did the original migration.
guidance_note: When switching package managers, grep the whole repo for `npm run`/`npm ci`/`npm publish` (scripts, comments, CI) and convert them all in one commit.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: 444c323 only changed a package.json script and a vite comment. The missing `subscribe`/`unsubscribe` on BridgePaneStreamClient dates from the original adapter. The bug was real: PaneStream skips size subscription and terminals stay 80x24.
guidance_note: When adapting a client to an interface with optional capabilities, list every optional method and decide each one explicitly, since a missing optional method compiles fine and silently disables a feature.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the constructor subscriptions are original adapter code, not from 444c323. The agent shows that the bridge and DemoStore live for the whole app and that DemoStore uses the same never-unsubscribe pattern, which is a sound reason not to change one consumer alone; the seam law adds nothing to that argument.

The flag is a false positive: the useMemo with its eslint-disable predates 444c323. As the agent notes, `paneStreamClient` is readonly and never changes for the store's lifetime, so there was no runtime bug, but declaring the dependency and dropping the suppression costs nothing.
guidance_note: Don't add an eslint-disable for exhaustive-deps to save a stable dependency; list the dependency.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: 9402598 touched PaneView.tsx and pane-stream-bridge.ts, not the bench, so `createSession()` is original code. Calling the void return of `client.on()` would throw, and running the bench surfaced two more bugs (`spawnTmux` called with an object as args, and `client.dispose()` on a class that only has `close()`).
guidance_note: Run every bench or test file you add at least once before opening the PR; this bench had three startup-breaking bugs because no script ran it.

evidence: The unescaped `refresh-client -B ${name}:${what}:'${format}'` was written in 9402598, the fix for F11. The F11 proposal chose "the same quoting pattern the demo already uses... in store.ts" over the `tmuxEscape` that TmuxClient.subscribe already uses. As the agent says, there is no injection risk today, but the canonical encoder existed.
guidance_note: When a fix builds a wire command that the library already builds elsewhere, reuse the library's encoder rather than a nearby hand-rolled pattern.

evidence: The F4/F8 fix (8c4d043) added `this.buffer = []` with no test; the agent's own eight-step trace was a ready-made test that went unwritten. abc49ed added it, asserting one seed and zero writes.
guidance_note: When a fix comes with a step-by-step reproduction, encode the reproduction as a regression test in the same commit.

evidence: abc49ed only added a unit test; the publish.yml npm-to-pnpm conversion is part of the package-manager switch that answered the lockfile threads. The packet does not show whether bare `pnpm publish` from this workspace root actually fails; the agent itself only said it was "fragile across pnpm versions".
guidance_note: When migrating a release workflow to a new package manager, run its publish step in dry-run mode before merging.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the `as unknown as OutputMessage` casts are in the round-6 hunk of the original adapter, and abc49ed only added a test. The agent notes the cast-free `subscription-changed` branch shows the discriminant already narrows correctly.
guidance_note: Treat `as unknown as` in new code as a signal to recheck the types; here the discriminant already did the narrowing.

narrative: This demo migration ran 12 Copilot rounds. Rounds 1 and 3 are duplicate passes on unchanged commits, and round 4 re-raised the lockfile issue the agent had deferred. Most later flags on fix commits are false positives on original code. The real fix-caused rounds were round 5 (incomplete npm-to-pnpm sweep), round 8 (the F11 subscribe fix hand-built an unescaped command instead of using tmuxEscape), and round 9 (the F4 buffer fix shipped without its regression test). F14 showed the demo bench had never been run.
guidance_observations: Deferring the lockfile decision to the user while resolving the thread cost three repeat findings; the branch later took the pnpm path anyway.
The bench added in this PR had three startup-breaking bugs because nothing ran it; running new test files once before review would have removed a round.
Several fixes (F4, F11) were correct in substance but missing a companion: a regression test, or reuse of the canonical encoder. Each gap cost a separate round.

evidence: TypeScript allows `typeof X` in type position on an `import type` class, so the claim that it would fail type-checking is wrong, and the agent said so while still simplifying to `X extends RpcProxyApi`. The agent's proof, "the build was actually green", is empty: #28/F3 later shows tests are not in the tsc build at all, so this gate was never checked in either form.
guidance_note: Before claiming a type-level test passes, mutate it to a failing assertion and confirm the build goes red; a gate outside the tsc graph is always green.

narrative: This PR was merged by automation without surfacing its single finding, then reverted (#27) and redone as #28. The finding's diagnosis was wrong, but it pointed at a conformance gate that #28 showed was never type-checked. The agent missed that because it took a green build as evidence.
guidance_observations: The address-pr-reviews automation merged before an open review thread was answered, so the whole PR had to be reverted and redone.

evidence: The agent bumped PROTOCOL_VERSION and split the envelope and protocol constants in 5f6d250. In a later issue comment it deleted all the versioning, because server and client ship in the same package before v0.1.0, so "the v1-client-connects-to-v2-server scenario... cannot occur". That bump then caused three follow-up findings (F4, F5, F6).
guidance_note: Before adding compatibility machinery a reviewer proposes, check whether two versions can actually ever meet (same package, same build, no releases); if they cannot, push back on the spot.

evidence: The constructor checks only `typeof this.client.subscribeRaw === "function"`, yet dispose() calls `unsubscribe` unconditionally, and both are optional on PaneStreamClient. The fix requires both, matching the `SubscriptionAwareClient` cast. The gap predates this PR (it existed under the name `subscribe`).
guidance_note: When a runtime capability check is followed by a cast to a type with several required members, check for every member the cast asserts.

evidence: The agent confirmed that tsconfig references only `src/**` and `packages/pane-terminal`, so the type-only assertion was erased unchecked, and replaced it with a pointer to the `implements RpcProxyApi` clauses that are in the build. The test was unchecked in its original form too, so the #26/F1 rewrite did not cause this.
guidance_note: When writing a compile-time gate, confirm the file is in the typecheck graph by breaking the assertion and watching the build fail.

evidence: The flag points at cb60903, which only removed the fake test, but the gap comes from the F1 fix (5f6d250): it bumped PROTOCOL_VERSION and split the envelope check while the only rejection test still sent `v: 999`. That test exercises the envelope path, so the bump had no test of its own. The added test was later deleted along with the versioning.
guidance_note: When a fix splits one check into two independent checks, add one test per check that triggers only that check.

evidence: The F1 bump changed websocket-transport.test.ts from `protocol: 1` to a hard-coded `protocol: 2`, while sibling tests import `PROTOCOL_VERSION`. The fix updated the literal instead of replacing it with the constant.
guidance_note: When bumping a constant, grep for the old literal value and replace each hit with the constant rather than the new literal.

evidence: The F1 fix wrote a history block saying "A v=1 client connecting to a v=2 server" in the same commit that made `v` the frame-envelope field fixed at 1. e30e4c4 later deleted the whole block along with the versioning.
guidance_note: When a fix gives a name a new, narrower meaning (here `v` = envelope), reread the comments the fix itself wrote for the old meaning.

narrative: This is a redo of #26. In round 0, the agent accepted a protocol-version bump (F1) for a bridge whose client and server always ship together. Rounds 1 and 2 came entirely from that bump: a missing behavior test, a hard-coded version literal, and a v=1/v=2 comment that contradicted the envelope split. The agent then stepped back and deleted the versioning, making all three moot. F2 and F3 were real fixes that survived.
guidance_observations: The agent's own issue comment, "three review iterations chasing downstream effects of one preemptive choice", is the lesson: test the premise of a reviewer's suggested machinery before adding it, not after two more rounds.
F3 showed that #26/F1's "the build was green" defense rested on a file the build never checks.
